searchText: Is this accurate? https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4036000 > We find that in our sample more than 75% of Byzantine actions have dodged penalty (slashing), highlighting that slashing may not be as effective as widely believed. If so, how is this happening? I thought only a single honest validator is required to enforce slashing? We have been discussing this internally between client teams and it appears they were basing the slashings on incorrect data. <@!361447803194441738> has a short doc in which he tries to recreate slashings for a few of these affected validators : https://hackmd.io/Bncoj0ilRfi6REyUJPWdiA Short version - all the data is based off of beaconcha.in rather than the chain itself and beaconcha.in has a couple of indexing bugs. None of the missed slashing are valid.
